summary: Walks a doubly-linked list starting at head this+0x1518, compares each node pointer against argument a2, and on a match unlinks that node by relinking prev->next and next->prev (node prev/next live at node+0x1C/+0x20). If the removed node is the head, advances the head to the removed node's next. Returns the matched node pointer, or the new head after a head removal, or 0 if the list is empty or a2 is not found. Legacy ABI label Doubly_Linked_List_Node_Unlink_by_Match; sole observed caller ResourceCascadeCleanup (0x005539F0).

operations.description: Load head from this+0x1518; if null the list is empty and the function returns 0 immediately.
Walk the list from head following each node's next pointer (node+0x20) until the node pointer equals a2; if the walk reaches a null next before matching, return 0.
Read prev pointer of the matched node from node+0x1C.
If the matched node's prev is non-null, write prev->next (prev+0x20) = matched->next so the previous node skips the removed node.
Read next pointer of the matched node from node+0x20.
If the matched node's next is non-null, write next->prev (next+0x1C) = matched->prev so the following node skips back over the removed node.
If the matched node equals the stored head, advance the head to the matched node's next and store it back at this+0x1518.
Return the matched node pointer; after a head removal the returned value is the new head (the removed node's next). Returns 0 when the list is empty or no node matches a2.
Invoked by ResourceCascadeCleanup (0x005539F0); this unlink-by-match is part of the resource cascade cleanup path.
Legacy ABI lead labels this routine Doubly_Linked_List_Node_Unlink_by_Match; the proposed name and function identity are anchored to that lead and the packet address.
